chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar Al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who went out during

the months of Hajj to perform Umra, then he returned to his country. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; and even if he performed Hajj in that year, and performed exclusive Hajj, so there is no blood (of a sacrificial animal) upon him, for Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) went out to Iraq one day before Al-Tarwiyya, and he had entered to perform Umra.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who performs Umra and then exclusive Hajj in the same year without combining them?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) rules that a man who performs Umra during the months of Hajj and then returns home, later performing exclusive Hajj in the same year, is not required to pay the blood (dam) of a sacrifice. This is based on the precedent of Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who performed Umra before departing for Iraq. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the combination of rituals, emphasizing that the Prophet's and Imams' practices serve as primary legal precedents for resolving specific ritual questions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamani, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about a man who went out during

the months of Hajj to perform Umra, then he returned to his city. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem; and even if performed Hajj during that year of his, and exclusive Hajj, so there is no blood (of a sacrificial animal) upon him, fro Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> went out to Al-Iraq before Al-Tarawiyya by a day, and he<sup>asws</sup> had entered to perform Umra’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yemaniy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about a man who travels in the months of al-Hajj for al-‘Umrah, then returns to his town. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful. If he performs al-Hajj in that year he is not required to offer animal offering. Al-Husayn ibn Ali, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, left before the day of al-Tarwiyah (eight of Dhu al-Hajj ah) for Iraq and he had entered Makkah for al-‘Umrah.’” NOTE: (Fatwa best explains Hadith 2-3 of this Chapter.)
